targetText: The same is true of fictitious capital, interest-bearing paper, in so far as it circulates on the stock exchange as money-capital.
explanation: Fictitious capital refers to financial paper assets (stocks, bonds, debt obligations) whose value represents claims on future surplus value rather than active physical production.

targetText: On the other hand, in so far as credit plays a direct role in the reproduction process, what the industrialist or merchant needs when he wishes to have a bill discounted or a loan granted is neither stocks nor government securities.
explanation: Commercial or merchant capital doesn’t create new surplus value directly, but collects a share of total social profit by speeding up the circulation and sale of goods.
